title: Where to Hire a Video Editor for Facebook Ads, Compared
summary: Hire a video editor for Facebook ads from a service, a studio or a freelancer. Compare editing scope, published prices and the paid test that proves the cut.
body_markdown:
A video editor for Facebook ads turns footage into vertical and square cuts with a hook, captions and a clean ending. You can hire an in-house editor, a freelancer, or a service that edits in batches. If you want finished ads and not an editor to manage, our top pick is[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/video-ad-production) , a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Facebook and Instagram. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What does a Facebook video editor have to get right?


Three details separate a usable Facebook edit from a repurposed file. The first is the frame. Meta's[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio and key messages kept inside the safe zone, clear of the Reels interface. The second is sound. The same page says Reels default to sound on, so plan the first second around audio, and add captions for viewers who watch muted.


The third is the bottom of the frame. Meta's[developer guide for Reels ads](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/creative/reels-ads) says to keep the bottom 35% of a 9:16 creative free of text, logos and other key elements. Feed uses a different shape. Meta's[Ads Guide for Facebook Feed](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/update/video) recommends 4:5 video at 1440 x 1800 pixels (checked October 2026). An editor who delivers one master has left you to crop the rest.


## Which providers can supply a Facebook video editor?


The table lists providers that publish editing work, with Knowlify first. The sources we checked do not publish hourly editor rates, so compare by the number of finished cuts and the monthly price.


Provider Editing scope (as published, October 2026) Published price Best fit


Knowlify Done-for-you AI video ads from one team, about 25 finished a week, with a person checking each ad From $5,000 a month; agreed target in 30 days on managed plans, 90-day refund on creative-only (terms on the site) Teams that want finished ads rather than an editor to manage


[Komet Media](https://www.kometmedia.com/services/instagram-ads) Turns webinars and podcasts into Reels, Stories and in-feed video ads $1,799 clips plan; monthly plans at $2,499 and $8,499 B2B SaaS and funded startups with long-form content to cut down


[Flighted](https://www.flighted.co/) In-house video editors and designers; says it makes more than 1,000 creatives a month Not published DTC brands spending $20K to $500K+ a month on paid social


[VideGro](https://www.videgro.co/) New videos built and reformatted for each platform Fixed fees, no percentage of ad spend; amounts not published Ecommerce brands that want fast iterations


[351 Studio](https://351studio.com/social-media-video-ads-production) Social video ads, or edits of your existing footage, with 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9 exports, captions and hooks Not published Teams that want human editors, with AI where it helps


[EditClub](https://www.editclub.co/) AI-generated actors and B-roll, with unlimited revisions and ownership of source files $1,600 to $4,000 a month for about 60 to 180 videos DTC brands spending $10K or more a month on Meta


### Knowlify: our top pick when you want finished ads, not an editor to manage


An editor needs footage, a brief and weekly feedback. Knowlify fits when you do not have footage to cut: it makes AI UGC with AI presenters talking to camera, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials for Facebook and Instagram, about 25 finished ads a week. The first batch lands on day five, and a person checks every ad before delivery, which is the review step you would otherwise run yourself.


You can buy creative only for a team with its own buyer, or add optional end-to-end Meta campaign management. Pricing is a custom quote, and if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Choose an editor instead when you already own footage that you want cut to your own voice and schedule.


### Komet Media: for turning long-form content into Reels and Stories


Komet Media calls itself a B2B video growth partner that works from existing podcasts, webinars and events, or builds video from scratch, for B2B SaaS, AI-native companies and funded startups. Its clips-only plan costs $1,799 and includes five clip edits. Its monthly plans are $2,499 for 10 clips a month and $8,499 for 30 or more pieces. It says its focus is the creative and does not say it runs campaigns, so confirm who buys the media.


### Flighted: for heavy-spend brands that want editors on a paid media team


Flighted lists in-house video editors and designers and says it makes more than 1,000 creatives a month. Its[about page](https://www.flighted.co/about) describes a New York paid media agency with Meta ads management, creative strategy and production, and structured creative testing. Fees are not published, and it says it works best with companies spending $50,000 or more a month on Meta, so it is a stretch for an early-stage budget.


### VideGro: for fast iterations on a fixed fee


VideGro describes paid social video for DTC and ecommerce brands, built around creating and iterating new videos quickly and reformatting them for each platform. Its fees are fixed, with no percentage of ad spend and expenses included. New videos can arrive in as little as 24 hours, while fully produced new concepts take days. Its homepage does not mention media buying, and exact prices are not published.


### 351 Studio: for several aspect ratios from one project


351 Studio's social video ads page says it can edit, enhance and adapt your existing footage, and delivers 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9 exports with captions and hooks. Typical pricing includes two revision rounds, and delivery takes 2 to 12 business days depending on scope. Its[AI video production page](https://351studio.com/ai-video-production) describes generative AI with human creative direction, editors and VFX artists. Pricing is not published, and its pages do not describe media buying.


### EditClub: for a high count of AI edits on a flat monthly price


EditClub describes itself as an on-demand creative team for DTC brands spending $10K or more a month on Meta, with no cameras and no creators. Its Crew plan costs $1,600 a month for about 60 videos with 72-hour delivery. Its Partner plan costs $4,000 for about 180 videos, with 24 to 48 hour delivery. Every plan lists unlimited revisions and ownership of your videos and source files.


## What belongs in an editor's scope?


Write the scope as a list of files, not hours. For each brief, name the number of cuts, the hook variants for the first three seconds, the caption file, the 9:16 and 4:5 exports, and the revision limit. Add who owns the project files, since EditClub, for example, states that you own your videos and source files, so ask every provider to state ownership in writing.


Also decide who writes the hook. An editor can cut a strong opening only when the brief names the claim it must carry. If you want the editor to propose hooks as well, say so and price it, because that is closer to a creative strategist's job than an editor's.
